sourcing_note: No individual speaker attributed in the primary write-up fetched (news.microsoft.com/source); stated as Microsoft's corporate position. Worth remembering when reading this claim back: Microsoft's own 2018 topological-qubit result (Nature) was retracted in 2021 after independent physicists could not reproduce it -- not evidence for or against THIS claim, but a reason the check-ins on this entry should demand unusually strong independent replication before crediting any interim milestone.
verbatim: the world's first quantum chip powered by a new Topological Core architecture that it expects will realize quantum computers capable of solving meaningful, industrial-scale problems in years, not decades.
headline: Microsoft says its Majorana 1 / Topological Core approach puts industrial-scale, meaningful quantum computing “years, not decades” away.
resolution_criteria: This claim names no specific year -- “years, not decades” is a hedge, not a deadline, so it fails intake rule 4 (deadlined) as stated. SymbiQ's own falsifiability construction, flagged as such rather than attributed to Microsoft: resolves NOT_VERIFIED if, by 19 Feb 2035 (ten years from the claim, the outer edge of what “years, not decades” can plausibly mean before it is simply wrong), no topological-qubit system from Microsoft has demonstrated a problem of genuine industrial scale and consequence that a classical computer could not also solve. VERIFIED if one has. This is deliberately a lenient, favourable-to-the-claimant reading of a vague sentence.
